amstar2_items.justification: No structured PICO/PEO research question or comparator is specified; eligibility criteria broadly cover rural drinking water interventions and the Jal Jeevan Mission (JJM), and even include a Kenyan study (Agesa & Agesa 2019) unrelated to JJM.
No pre-registered or pre-specified written protocol (e.g., PROSPERO or OSF) is reported, and no protocol deviations are addressed.

Section 3.4 states that scholarly articles, review papers, and book chapters were included, without justifying the selection of study designs or the mixing of empirical studies with policy commentaries/reviews.

Although multiple databases/platforms and keywords are named, no full Boolean search strings or database-specific queries are provided, grey literature and non-English studies were excluded without justification, and an arbitrary 20-article stopping rule was applied to Google Scholar.
Section 3.1 reports that records were screened independently by the authors on titles/abstracts and full texts, with disagreements resolved through discussion among the authors.

Author contributions (p. 13) state that data collection and analysis were performed by a single author (Malini Srinivasan), with subsequent review of NVivo coding by co-authors rather than independent duplicate data extraction.
Four full-text articles were reportedly excluded at the eligibility stage, but no bibliographic list of excluded full-text studies with individual exclusion reasons is provided.

Table 1 lists only author names and titles (with a broken reference pointer for S. No. 10), providing no per-study details on populations, sample sizes, study designs, comparators, settings, or outcomes.

No formal risk-of-bias or critical appraisal tool (e.g., ROBINS-I, MMAT, CASP, JBI) was used; Section 3.9 states only that publications from 'reliable and reputed scholarly journals and books' were read by the three authors.
Sources of funding for the 20 included studies are not reported anywhere in the review.
No quantitative synthesis or meta-analysis was performed; the review used qualitative thematic analysis in NVivo 12.
Risk of bias in individual studies was neither formally assessed nor accounted for when interpreting thematic findings or formulating policy conclusions.

While regional implementation disparities across Indian states are narratively noted, methodological heterogeneity across study designs (surveys, case studies, policy commentaries, and an uncited Kenyan study) is neither explained nor analyzed.
No quantitative synthesis was conducted, so publication/small-study bias was not statistically investigated.
The authors explicitly report their funding source (Indian Council of Social Science Research, ICSSR) and declare no competing interests on page 14.

methodological_notes: Although titled a PRISMA 2020 'Systematic review' (SLR), this paper is methodologically a low-rigour qualitative thematic/scoping synthesis (NVivo 12) of 20 heterogeneous sources including empirical surveys/case studies, secondary policy commentaries, and a book chapter, making AMSTAR 2 only borderline-applicable and yielding Critically Low confidence (5 critical flaws: Q2, Q4, Q7, Q9, Q13). Multiple internal reporting anomalies exist: (1) Section 2 lists 5 databases/platforms whereas Section 3.1 lists 8 (including publisher platforms Elsevier/ScienceDirect counted separately and ResearchGate); (2) Section 3.5 states 62 database records yielded 24 unique records after deduplication, whereas Section 4 states 62 database records plus 8 citation-chasing records (70 total) yielded the same 24 records; (3) Google Scholar was truncated at 20 hits; (4) the search window began in January 2002 even though Jal Jeevan Mission launched in 2019, resulting in pre-JJM or non-JJM inclusions such as a 2019 study of women fetching water in Kenya (Agesa & Agesa [13], never cited in the Results); (5) Table 1 S. No. 10 ('Kumar & Goyal [9]') erroneously duplicates reference number [9] (Ranjeet Kumar 2024) and lacks a reference list entry; (6) Table 3 research method counts sum to 23 across 20 included studies; and (7) PRISMA 2020 (Page et al. 2021) is cited twice as Ref [1] and Ref [4]. On scope (Criterion 2), the review is primarily a broad programme evaluation of JJM (socio-economic/gender, health, infrastructure), touching only secondarily on local administrative governance (Gram Panchayat roles, contractor/local-government responsibility ambiguity, and missing grievance redressal mechanisms), so it is rated borderline_narrow_c2. References [25]-[32] appear only as external comparative/discussion citations in Sections 6.2, 6.4, 6.6, and 7 and are excluded from the 20 synthesized studies in Table 1.
